conversation.text: Hey, need your input on MR-JE-AX167 on Line 11, machining cell B. Operator keeps hearing a grinding noise from the HG servo motor during Z-axis rapid traverse, about three times a shift since Monday. No alarm, drive runs fine otherwise, and it only happens when the axis moves.
Any vibration or just noise? And the noise stops when the machine is idle, right?
Yeah, quiet when it's sitting still. Records say the motor's from 2019, around 21,000 running hours. I was thinking maybe encoder's going bad, should we just swap the whole motor out?
Hold on, don't jump to the encoder. On this cell, bearing noise on MR-JE-AX167 usually first shows up between 18,000 and 22,000 motor running hours. You're right in that window.
Okay, so how do I confirm it before pulling anything apart?
Before you remove the load, jog MR-JE-AX167 at 50 mm/min and listen with a stethoscope right at the motor flange. That'll tell you if it's the bearing or the machine.
And if the bearing is the problem, can we just repair it here on the line?
No, if the bearing is suspect, tag the motor and send it to the Binh Duong workshop for replacement, not local repair.
Got it. What about checking the shaft by hand? Someone said we could spin it while it's still hooked up.
Don't do that. Always disconnect the motor power cable and wait 15 minutes before rotating the shaft by hand to release the brake safely.
And what if I spin it and hear nothing?
Then the motor's fine and you go maintain the machine itself. But if it makes noise when you turn it by hand, bearing's worn and the motor gets replaced.
One more thing, someone suggested tweaking the servo amplifier gain parameters to kill the noise. Worth trying?
No, don't touch the gain to hide a noise. Check the bearing first, that's the real issue here.

followUp.text: Follow-up on MR-JE-AX167, Line 11, machining cell B. Jogged at 50 mm/min with the stethoscope on the motor flange. The grinding is clearly coming from the motor.
Did you check the shaft by hand?
Yes. Disconnected the motor power cable, waited 15 minutes, then turned the shaft by hand. It grinds when turned by hand.
Then the bearing's worn. Tag it and send it to the Binh Duong workshop.
Done. Motor tagged and sent to Binh Duong. Replacement motor installed, Z-axis rapid traverse ran two full shifts with no grinding noise. Gain parameters untouched.
Good. Log it so the next person checks the bearing first.

Author: expert_01 (senior technician)

- On this cell, bearing noise on MR-JE-AX167 usually first shows up between
  18,000 and 22,000 motor running hours.
- Bearing or machine? Jog at 50 mm/min before removing the load and listen
  at the motor flange with a stethoscope.
- Never rotate the shaft by hand while the motor is connected. Disconnect the
  motor power cable and wait 15 minutes first, to release the brake safely.
- Noise when turned by hand: bearing worn, replace the motor.
  No noise: the motor is fine, maintain the machine.
- Suspect bearing: tag the motor, send it to Binh Duong workshop for
  replacement. No local repair.
- Do not change servo gain to hide a noise.
